contract_findings: SCOPE of this list: every item is read from the bytes and proved PER CALL (one successful call implies ...). No item is a theorem over a sequence of calls, and nothing here reads the live chain state (who holds a role today is not known to the proofs).

Mint, per call: a mint(to, amount) that ends with no error was sent by the address in slot 11 (the minter) at the time of that call (ok_mint, mint_readable; no keccak hypothesis); to must not be 0; no cap in the bytecode; totalSupply add is checked, the balance add is unchecked (safe under the invariant). NOT a theorem: "the total supply never grows except in such a mint". It follows by reading the other readable theorems one by one (some under Sep); no single Lean statement says it (the ten-token audit, USDE-6).

Minter change, per call: a setMinter(newMinter) that ends with no error was sent by the owner (slot 0); no delay, no zero check (the owner can set the minter to 0, which stops minting, or to itself); emits MinterUpdated. So the minter is not a lasting fact: the owner key alone is enough to mint any amount in two calls.

Owner change: two steps (Ownable2Step): owner calls transferOwnership(new) which only writes _pendingOwner (slot 1) and logs OwnershipTransferStarted; the pending owner calls acceptOwnership, which writes _owner, clears _pendingOwner and logs OwnershipTransferred. Slots 0 and 1 keep their 96 high bits.
renounceOwnership() always reverts (proved: renounceOwnership_never; ok_renounceOwnership : False).
burn(amount) burns the caller's balance; burnFrom(account, amount) spends allowance (infinite allowance is not reduced). Supply moves by exactly the amount (supply invariant).
No pause, no blacklist, no fee, no hook: transfer/transferFrom move exactly the amount.

transaction_theorems.file: UsdeVerify/Usde/Tx.lean (171 lines, 10 theorems, 1 abbrev QMsg), on the shared library TokenKit/Seq (Frame, Run, Tx, Supply)
transaction_theorems.headline: supply_any_transactions: after any finite list of transactions (Seq.Chain) that EthLib's processTransaction runs, whoever sends them, whatever they call and however deep (calls back into USDe included), C still holds the code of USDe and the supply invariant Inv C holds, when both held on the block state before the first one. Every selector is included: supply_permit (PermitSeq.lean) for permit, supply_preserved (Invariant.lean) for every other selector.
transaction_theorems.supply_message_any_depth: one call run by EthLib's processMessage, to any account and any code, at any depth: 'C holds the code of USDe and the invariant holds' is kept, with or without an error. Paris <= fork < Glamsterdam. Assumes Seq.Sane (a call that runs at C runs CODE), Seq.Good at the start, Seq.Clean of this run with Q := QMsg fork.
transaction_theorems.supply_transaction: one whole transaction run by EthLib's processTransaction (gas purchase, EIP-7702 authorizations, the message, call or creation, refunds, fee, deletion of accounts): block state before to block state after. Dencun <= fork < Glamsterdam. Assumes Seq.TxClean of this transaction and Seq.Good at the start.
transaction_theorems.supply_any_transactions: the same after any finite list of transactions (Seq.Chain), each at its own fork (Dencun <= fork < Glamsterdam) and in its own block environment.
transaction_theorems.supply_from_zero: the same from the base case shape: C holds the code and every storage word of C is zero (inv_zeroBase); conclusion Inv C after the list. This is NOT the real deployment state of USDe (the constructor run is not verified).
transaction_theorems.frameKeepsR: the per-frame premise of the library (Seq.FrameKeepsR: a frame that runs CODE at C under EthLib's real runner processRunner and ends with no error keeps Inv C), proved from the existing all-selector theorems: supply_permit (PermitSeq.lean) for permit, supply_preserved (Invariant.lean) for every other selector. Paris <= fork < Glamsterdam, any gas cap. No hypothesis on the runner is left: the STATICCALL to the ecrecover precompile is a message of the run like any other and the library induction covers it.
transaction_theorems.fork_range: transaction theorems: Fork.dencun <= fork < Fork.glamsterdam for each transaction. Message theorem: Fork.paris <= fork < Fork.glamsterdam.
transaction_theorems.start_state: Seq.Good C CODE (Inv C) on the block state before the first transaction (assumed, see assumptions); supply_from_zero: Seq.HoldsCode plus all-zero storage of C.
transaction_theorems.older_model_kept: Seq.lean and PermitSeq.lean (inv_calls, inv_callsP, process_step, process_step_all, process_step_all_inv, calls_process, callsP_process): top-level messages only, where every other step is ASSUMED to keep the storage of C (the constructor `other` with `Untouched`). This is the weaker per-message model. It is kept because other files and the axioms list use it; the theorems of Tx.lean do not use that assumption.

fork_range.headline: Every claim of this file is for Paris <= fork < Glamsterdam (transactions: Dencun <= fork < Glamsterdam). Nothing is claimed for Glamsterdam or later.
fork_range.why: The proofs use the one-counter gas meter (Evm fork Nat). EthLib runs that meter only before Glamsterdam; from Glamsterdam it runs the two-counter meter of EIP-8037, which is not ported.
fork_range.stated_in_the_theorem: fork < .glamsterdam is a hypothesis of: ok_permit_real, permit_readable, supply_permit, process_step_all, process_step_all_inv, permitCall_process, callsP_process, frameKeepsR, supply_message_any_depth, supply_transaction, supply_any_transactions, supply_from_zero (Tx.lean), and of every theorem of Instance.lean and PermitRun.lean that is about a run (supply_m0, ecrecover_call_runs, permit_runs, supply_permit_m1, permit_runs_inv).
fork_range.not_stated_in_the_theorem: The older generated theorems (block rules, path specs, ok_<fn>, supply_<fn>, supply_preserved, <fn>_readable, the Sanity witnesses) and the hand-written older per-message model of Seq.lean (process_step, process_step_inv, calls_process) carry only the lower bound (Berlin <= fork; Seq.lean from Paris). They are statements about the one-counter model and are true as stated at every such fork, but they describe what EthLib really runs only before Glamsterdam. The bound was NOT added to them: it would have to come from the generators in token-kit/scripts (shared by every token, outside the scope of this fix round), and adding a hypothesis that the proofs do not use would change no proof. Read each of them with fork < Glamsterdam; every headline that reaches a message or a transaction (the lists above) states it.

closed_instance.audit: the ten-token audit, fix 5 (USDE-2): PARTLY closed
closed_instance.plain_answer: There is NO closed instance of Sep, and so no theorem under Sep (supply_<fn>, supply_preserved, supply_permit, the readable theorems of the writers, the sequence and transaction theorems) has an instance with every hypothesis proved. Each open fact of Sep says that a given slot is the balance slot keccak(a, 2) of no address word a: a statement over 2^160 values of keccak. keccak is a real function here, but no proof can run it 2^160 times and no shorter argument is known (it is preimage and collision resistance). Under the usual random-function view each fact fails with chance about 2^-96.
closed_instance.state_and_call: state sState C []: one account at the contract C, every storage word 0. Call m0: allowance(K, K) sent by HOLDER, the address with the word K = 0x19e7e376e7c213b7e7e7e46cc70a5dd086daff2a (the address of the public test key 0x11...11), so the three mapping keys of the call are K, K, K.
proved_with_no_hypothesis: inv_start: the start invariant Inv holds in that state (sum of balances 0, total supply 0)
callKeys_m0, callKeys_m1: the keys of the two calls are [K, K, K]
computed by the kernel with the real keccak: allow_ne_total, nonce_ne_total, allow_ne_nonce, slots_not_fixed
sep_iff, sep_m0_iff: Sep [K, K, K] holds exactly when KeyFacts holds (both directions), so the list of 7 facts below is the whole open part and cannot be made shorter
left_as_hypothesis: KeyFacts.total: slot 4 (the total supply) is the balance slot keccak(a, 2) of no address word a
KeyFacts.uniq: no address word other than K has the balance slot of K
KeyFacts.allow: the allowance slot of (K, K) is the balance slot of no address word
KeyFacts.nonce: the nonce slot of K (mapping at slot 9) is the balance slot of no address word
KeyFacts.slot0: slot 0 is the balance slot of no address word

owner_facts.source: the ten-token audit, finding USDE-9: facts about the deployed bytes that the auditor confirmed and that matter to an owner or a user. Each is per call; none is a statement about live chain state.
facts: USDE-9.1: mint has no cap and one gate, caller = slot 11. The owner (slot 0) can set slot 11 to any address at any time with setMinter (no delay, no zero check), so the owner key alone is enough to mint any amount in two calls. Treat the owner key as a mint key.
USDE-9.2: renounceOwnership always fails (renounceOwnership_never, any runner), so that power can only move by the two-step transfer, never be dropped.
USDE-9.3: transfer and transferFrom check only to != 0; to may be the token's own address, and none of the 25 selectors can move tokens out of it, so tokens sent to the contract are stuck.
USDE-9.4: with an allowance of 2^256-1, transferFrom and burnFrom do not lower it, emit no Approval log and skip the 'caller != 0' check.

USDE-9.5: permit has no check of v in the bytes; a bad v is rejected only because ECRECOVER returns nothing and the output word was 0 before the call. s in the upper half is rejected. The nonce is written before the call and its add is unchecked.

USDE-9.6: the cached domain separator in the code equals the rebuilt hash for chain id 1 and the deployed address, with name hash keccak('USDe') and version '1'; on another chain id or under DELEGATECALL the separator is rebuilt.
USDE-9.7: no external call other than the STATICCALL to address 1: no reentrancy surface, no hook, no pause, no blacklist, no fee.

USDE-9.8: the balance add in transfer / transferFrom / mint and the supply sub in burn / burnFrom are unchecked in the bytes and are safe only because of the invariant (transfer_no_wrap, mint_no_wrap, burn_no_wrap).
